question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay that wins over mutable config and blocks weakening writes, or keep immutable baseline handling in Policy/Nix-style conformance surfaces?
rationale: This choice changes security boundaries, config precedence, startup behavior, write rejection, and operator recovery paths; current main only has adjacent conformance checks and narrow config-write guards.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Add a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hook design settles
options.body: Keep this issue open while related policy-hook proposals clarify whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks, core config/write paths, or both.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Add a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns this maintainer issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest decision owner for the security-boundary direction.
